sources.citation: Harley, Matthew. 2020. Aspects of the phonology and morphosyntax of Kyak, an Adamawa language of Nigeria. Language in Africa 1(3): 373-404. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-373-404
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Sister language Kyak [bka], not Mak: tone language (§3.3 tones, floating L, downstep); no stress statement; Mak mentioned only in classification (p.377).

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Nlabephee Othaniel. 2020. The Jen language cluster: A comparative analysis of wordlists. Language in Africa 1(3): 17-99. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-17-99 (open access at iling-ran.ru)
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative phonology of 10 Jen varieties incl. Mak (Lee Mak of Panya and Zoo); prosody covered = nasalisation, tone (H, M, L, falling, rising; §3.3 p.43, Table 20 p.45), breathy voice. Mak forms are tone-marked throughout. Words 'stress'/'accent' absent from the 83-page PDF.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Nlabephee Othaniel. 2019. The Jen cluster: comparative analysis of wordlists. Slides, Adamawa Conference, Mainz, 9-11 Sept 2019.
sources.note: Nothing; slide version of the 2020 paper (vowels, nasalisation, consonants, classification). Notes 'occasional allophonic variants in Mak s̪ l̪ x for s l k'. No stress/accent.
